data.question: Of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World, just one still stands, and it was also the oldest of them. Which?
data.explanation: The Great Pyramid of Giza. The oldest wonder outlasting the rest is the giveaway.
data.answer_full: The Great Pyramid of Giza. The oldest wonder outlasting the rest is the giveaway.

data.question: The Rosetta Stone repeats one decree in three scripts. Two are Egyptian, hieroglyphic and Demotic. Given who ruled Egypt after Alexander, what is the third?
data.explanation: Ancient Greek. The Ptolemies, Greek-speaking successors of Alexander, ruled Egypt.
data.answer_full: Ancient Greek. The Ptolemies, Greek-speaking successors of Alexander, ruled Egypt.

data.question: Julius Caesar crossed the Rubicon and was assassinated within five years. Was it the 3rd, 2nd or 1st century BC?
data.explanation: 1st century BC. He crossed in 49 BC and was killed in 44 BC.
data.answer_full: 1st century BC. He crossed in 49 BC and was killed in 44 BC.

data.question: Hadrian's Wall marked the northern frontier of which empire, and was it begun in the 1st, 2nd or 3rd century AD?
data.explanation: The Roman Empire, 2nd century AD (begun about AD 122). Emperor Hadrian reigned AD 117 to 138.
data.answer_full: The Roman Empire, 2nd century AD (begun about AD 122). Emperor Hadrian reigned AD 117 to 138.

data.question: The ancient Olympic Games were held at Olympia, with a gap between Games that gave Greeks a unit of time called an Olympiad. Was the gap 2, 4 or 5 years?
data.explanation: 4 years. The modern Games kept the same rhythm.
data.answer_full: 4 years. The modern Games kept the same rhythm.
